reader_question: Where did each 2024 presidential nominee’s joint fundraising committee send what it raised?
grade_line: Documented: the committees’ reports to the Federal Election Commission
title: The Harris Victory Fund sent $899.5 million to 55 committees in the 2024 cycle, and the Trump National Committee JFC sent $273.8 million to two.
measure_line: Dollars each 2024 presidential nominee’s joint fundraising committee paid to other committees, 2023 to 2024 election cycle, not adjusted for inflation; a link’s width is its dollars, on one scale for both
notes: Each nominee had more than one joint fundraising committee. Each drawn here is the one that sent its nominee’s campaign the most, read the same way for both; the nominees’ other such committees sent the Harris campaign $4.9 million and the Trump campaign $160.9 million.
A joint fundraising committee raises money for several committees at once and splits it among them by agreement, so a transfer passes on money raised for the committee that gets it.
The 51 state party committees include the District of Columbia’s. The table lists each committee paid, with the report lines the payments were filed on.
alt: Two committees side by side, each a box with links to the committees it paid, each link as wide as its dollars on one scale. The Harris Victory Fund sent $528.7 million to the Harris campaign, $189.3 million to the Democratic National Committee, $181.4 million to 51 state party committees and $81,000 to two other committees. The Trump National Committee JFC sent $246.8 million to the Trump campaign and $26.9 million to the Republican National Committee.
chart_notes: Both committees are drawn alike, in one ink, on one scale of widths. A link under $4 million draws one pixel wide, so the $81,000 to two other committees shows as a hairline.

notes_internal: Maker B, round 3. Data plan row 94 with change 8, rule 14.104. Draws fec-jfc-transfers-2024 (P7-216): for each nominee the joint fundraising committee that sent the most to the principal campaign committee, read the same way for both, and every committee it paid.

Data lead ruling (a): no named mark, both committees as a set; (b): both drawn alike, side by side from 680 px (one under the other below, each source's words heading its block under 420 px); every node edge and link in the party-mark ink (money spent to elect a candidate, Rule 14.6's list), node words in the text's ink; one linear unit for both, $4 million a pixel, with a key of three widths and a hairline line; Harris's 51 state party committees fold into one node and the table lists each with its Schedule B lines.

Node names give each campaign in 2024's words (Harris for President; Donald J. Trump for President 2024), since the FEC lists the two principal committees today by different conventions; the research lead's RL-3 makes the table read alike.
